## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR should not merge yet. It deletes `app/defaults.json`, which `app/startup.py` still loads, and `is_valid_port` rejects port 65535. `load_config` hides every error behind `{}`, and the `normalize_host` docstring does not match what the function returns. No project policy files are listed in the manifest.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — This PR deletes `app/defaults.json`, but `app/startup.py:6` still reads it with `json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text())`. Nothing in the diff updates or replaces `load_defaults()`. Should the file be restored, or should `load_defaults` be changed in this PR to work without it? — Every call to `load_defaults()` will now raise `FileNotFoundError`, so startup can no longer read its default `{"timeout":30}`.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `return 0 < p < 65535` returns `False` for `p = 65535`, but the docstring on line 21 says the valid range is "(1-65535)". Could you change it to `0 < p <= 65535` and add `assert is_valid_port(65535)` and `assert not is_valid_port(65536)` to `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound`? — Port 65535 is a legal TCP port, but it would be rejected as unusable.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `except Exception: return {}` turns every failure into an empty config with no log and no signal to the caller. That includes `FileNotFoundError` from a mistyped path, `PermissionError`, and the JSON decode error raised for a malformed file such as `{"timeout": 5,`. There is also no comment next to it saying the fallback is intentional. Could you narrow the catch to `FileNotFoundError`, or at least log the exception, and let parse errors reach the caller? — If a config file is broken or unreadable, the code quietly runs on built-in defaults and the operator gets no clue why their settings were ignored.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says "returns None when h is empty", but lines 36–37 do `if h == "": return ""`. Which behavior do you want? Either return `None` or change the docstring to say it returns `""`. — A caller that follows the docstring and checks `normalize_host(h) is None` will never catch empty input and will pass `""` on as a hostname.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — No test covers the trailing-dot branch (`if lowered.endswith("."): lowered = lowered[:-1]`). `test_normalize_host_lowercases` only passes `"Example.COM"`. Could you add a case like `normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`? — If that branch broke, for example by stripping every trailing dot or none, no test would fail, even though stripping one trailing dot is one of the two documented behaviors.

## Strengths
- `test_parse_timeout_millis` covers the new `ms` branch in `parse_timeout` and asserts the result in seconds (`"1500ms"` → `1.5`), which matches the "timeout in seconds" docstring.
- The optional `ujson` import falls back to the standard-library `json`, and an adjacent comment explains the fallback.

(none)
